evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 75: vīta haec rūstica, quam tū agrestem vocās (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 16.21.7: rūsticus Rōmānus factus es
terms.comment: Of the country and of farming (rēs rūstica, agriculture); of people it is also plain, unsophisticated, and sometimes boorish, as against urbānus. For “in the country” say rūrī (see countryside).
Of the land and the fields; of wild plants (see wild, of plants); and of people, more often than rūsticus, uncouth, coarse.

phrases.latin: ōlim rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō, veterem vetus hospes amīcum
phrases.english: once upon a time, they say, a country mouse welcomed a town mouse in his poor hole, an old host his old friend

phrases.latin: nam rēs rūstica sīc est, sī ūnam rem sērō fēceris, omnia opera sērō faciēs
phrases.english: for farming is like this: if you do one job late, you will do every job late
you have become a Roman countryman
